answer_1.quote: What led Reiter and Thomson (2020) to launch a shared task competition in 2020 was a concern that fact-checking automatically generated texts (machine texts, or M TEXTs) in the context of data to text generation (Wiseman et al., 2017), is hugely labor intensive, making it virtually impossible to run it at a scale.
answer_1.outputs: M TEXTs (machine-generated texts) in the context of data-to-text generation

answer_2.quote: your goal is to locate factual mistakes in M TEXTs and classify them according to a pre-defined scheme of error types ('word,' 'number,' 'name,', 'context,' 'not checkable').
